source.title: The Curious Case of Benign Memorization
source.authors: Sotiris Anagnostidis; Gregor Bachmann; Lorenzo Noci; Thomas Hofmann

page_placements.theme: Useful internal information can survive corrupted predictions

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reproduces random-label training results and measures learned representations with K-NN and linear probes, including experiments with data augmentation; its central representation measures differ from the original random-label test.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own random-label fitting results and representation probes. Results attributed to Zhang et al. (2017), including training-time comparisons and regularizer claims, are cited background and are not extracted as this paper's results. Figure-only curves are not converted into numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study repeats random-label training and directly reports perfect training accuracy, matching the original randomization method and fitting measure. Its representation probes address a separate question. It also tests augmentation's compatibility with memorization and reports its own optimization comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. With augmentation, networks memorize random labels while learning useful encoder features, with noisy memorization concentrated in the projector. The authors propose that inflated sample size and limited capacity force exploitation of correlated augmentations and invariance learning; they do not claim a complete established explanation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it reproduces a subset of Zhang et al. (2017)'s results, then adds data augmentation and representation probing. Its CIFAR and TinyImageNet experiments use ResNet18 and VGG11 configurations and report K-NN and linear-probe results.
record.method_sensitivity: Data augmentation changes the representation outcome: clean-label K-NN probe accuracy after random-label training is much higher with standard augmentation than without it. The paper also reports that augmentation diversity and strength affect probing performance; those plots do not provide extractable exact values here.

fits_no_version.finding: Augmented random-label training improves clean-label K-NN embedding accuracy over initialization across both architectures and all three datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label training with suitable augmentation can learn useful representations while memorizing the training labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Without augmentation, ResNet18's CIFAR10 embedding K-NN accuracy falls from 40.2% to 12.4%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label training without augmentation can degrade the usefulness of learned embeddings.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean and random-label probes separate sharply between encoder and projector layers under augmentation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature learning and noisy-label memorization can be distributed across different network layers.

record.problems: The text gives no separate numeric training-accuracy values for the reproduced random-label conditions; it states that training accuracy is perfect. Many training dynamics and noise-sweep outcomes appear only in figures, without extractable exact values. The study changes the training protocol with data augmentation in its central experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted under the 60-row limit. Figure-only results include the convergence curves in Figure 4, label-noise and transfer sweeps in Figures 10–13, and augmentation-strength results in Figure 12; exact values are not extracted from those plots.

untested.parts: An unchanged training budget between clean and random labels is not established; augmented random-label training takes substantially longer. The models use modified encoders and large MLP projectors. Chance-level classifier test performance is stated for unaugmented training, but is not separately quantified across all augmented conditions.
No numerical clean/random convergence-time ratio is given. The corruption-fraction curves in Figure 11 measure K-NN feature quality, not convergence of fitting the noisy training targets.
No fitting experiment on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or wholly Gaussian-noise inputs. The toy example contains class signal and is not this test.
The corruption sweeps measure embedding probes, not the trained classifier's joint training fit and test error across corruption fractions.

No controlled weight-decay or dropout comparison, and no direct trained-classifier test of how removing regularizers affects clean-label generalization. Table 6 specifies zero weight decay and no dropout.
Layer-wise signal/noise separation and clean-label probing over time do not establish that shared real-label patterns are fitted before noisy targets.

missing.what: The study's own clean-versus-random training-loss comparison reports no significant fitting slowdown without augmentation; the record incorrectly treats training-time comparisons as exclusively cited background.

The explicit comparison stating substantially increased training time with augmented random labels is not captured by a row. Figure 4 is declared omitted, but this textual comparison is independently available.
missing.locator: Section 4, Benign Memorization, paragraph discussing training time

missing.what: Random-label fitting becomes infeasible within the fixed 5000-epoch budget as independently labeled augmentation multiplicity increases.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Inflated Sample Size; Figure 6, training-loss panel

missing.what: Projector-width experiments identify a threshold below which learning is impossible or very difficult within the fixed computational budget; extract the fitting outcome separately from K-NN quality.
missing.locator: Appendix C, Role of the Projector; Figure 8

record.verdict_notes: Useful clean-label probes do not contradict chance-level performance of the trained random-label classifier. Perfect augmented-condition accuracy is evaluated on original, unaugmented training images. Appendix F specifies Adam, MSE loss, a 65536-wide projector, no dropout, and zero weight decay. Section 7 explicitly states that code was released, contrary to the record's metadata.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports fitting under random labels with and without data augmentation, but does not establish that its full training setup and hyperparameters match the original settings.
The paper cites a prior training-time comparison but does not report its own comparison of training time for clean versus random labels or convergence speed by corruption fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment is reported.
The label-noise sweep reports K-NN probing performance, not the trained network's training fit and test error across corruption levels.

Weight decay and dropout claims are attributed to prior work; the study does not test whether these regularizers prevent random-label fitting or whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
The study measures signal and noise across layers, but does not test whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.
